issues.description: RevokeErr exposed via API may leak sensitive backend/system details
issues.detail: The PR author explicitly raised this concern. RevokeErr originates from arbitrary backend revocation failures and may contain connection strings, internal hostnames, credentials in URLs, or stack traces. Exposing it through the lease lookup API (which is callable by lower-privilege holders depending on policy) widens the attack surface. Consider gating behind sudo capability or sanitizing.

issues.description: API capability/policy implications of returning namespace_path and path not considered
issues.detail: Returning `path` and `namespace_path` allows a caller with only a lease ID to discover the mount path and namespace of any lease they hold the ID for. This could enable information disclosure across namespaces in multi-tenant setups. The PR should document and test the ACL implications, especially the cross-namespace case.

issues.description: Breaking rename of exported method FetchLeaseTimes without deprecation shim
issues.detail: FetchLeaseTimes is an exported method on ExpirationManager. Renaming it to FetchLeaseInfo is a breaking change for any external consumer importing vault as a library (plugins, forks, downstream tooling). A deprecation wrapper that delegates to FetchLeaseInfo would preserve compatibility for one release cycle.

issues.description: namespace field copied by reference but not documented as immutable
issues.detail: leaseInfoForExport copies `le.namespace` by pointer into the returned struct. If callers mutate the returned namespace or if the namespace pointer is later modified, this leaks shared state. Other fields (IssueTime, ExpireTime, Path) are values; namespace breaks the pattern. Document immutability or copy the relevant Path field only.

issues.description: Test coverage missing for new namespace_path and revoke_error fields
issues.detail: The added test in logical_system_test.go only asserts `path`. There is no test verifying `namespace_path` is populated for a non-root namespace lease, nor that `revoke_error` surfaces correctly when revocation has failed. Without these, regressions in the namespace or revoke-error paths will go undetected.

issues.description: Metric label still labeled fetch-lease-times after rename
issues.detail: The metric key `expire.fetch-lease-times` was preserved when renaming to FetchLeaseInfo. This is actually correct for metric continuity, but should be noted/commented so future maintainers don't "fix" the inconsistency and break dashboards/alerts that depend on the existing metric name.

review.summary: The PR cleanly extends lease lookup with path, namespace_path, and revoke_error. The main concern, which the author raised themselves, is that RevokeErr from arbitrary backends may contain sensitive content and is now reachable via API. Returning path/namespace_path also has multi-tenant disclosure implications worth checking. Secondary concerns: the rename of an exported method without a shim is a breaking change for downstream consumers, the namespace pointer is shared rather than deep-copied, and the new fields lack dedicated test coverage beyond the basic path assertion.
